What This Calculator Actually Does

Running AI at scale costs real money. Whether you're processing thousands of documents, running automated pipelines, or querying language models continuously, the bill adds up — and it adds up differently depending on which provider you use, which model you pick, and how you structure your requests.

This calculator gives you a straightforward way to compare costs across the main LLM providers before you commit to a particular approach. Put in your expected usage, and it shows you what each option is likely to cost. No assumptions hidden in the background. No vendor preference baked in.

Why Provider Costs Vary So Much

LLM pricing is not straightforward. Providers charge differently based on input tokens, output tokens, context window size, and whether you're using a base model or a fine-tuned variant. Some charge per request. Others charge per token. Some offer batch pricing that's significantly cheaper for non-urgent workloads.

The same task — say, summarising a 2,000-word document — can cost ten times more on one provider than another, depending on how you structure the prompt and which model you use. That gap matters when you're running the task ten thousand times a month.

The Main Cost Variables

  • Input tokens: The text you send to the model, including your prompt, any context, and retrieved documents if you're using RAG.
  • Output tokens: The text the model generates in response. Generally more expensive per token than input.
  • Model tier: Frontier models (the most capable) cost significantly more than mid-tier or smaller models. For many tasks, the cheaper model is good enough.
  • Context window: Larger context windows cost more per call. If your use case doesn't need a 128k context window, don't pay for one.
  • Batch vs. real-time: Some providers offer batch APIs at half the price for workloads that don't need an immediate response.

How to Use This Calculator

Start with your expected monthly volume — how many requests, roughly how long each prompt is, and how long you expect the responses to be. If you're not sure, the calculator includes some common use case templates to give you a starting point.

The output shows you a monthly cost estimate for each provider and model combination. It also flags where the cost difference between options is significant enough to warrant a closer look at whether a cheaper model would meet your needs.

A note on estimates: These figures are based on publicly listed API pricing and are updated regularly, but provider pricing changes. Always verify current rates directly with the provider before making budget decisions. This calculator is for planning and comparison — not invoicing.

Choosing the Right Model, Not Just the Cheapest One

The lowest cost option is not always the right option. A cheaper model that gets the task wrong 15% of the time costs more in downstream errors than a more expensive model with higher accuracy. The goal is cost-effectiveness, which means matching the model to the task.

Some rules of thumb that hold up in practice:

  • Simple classification, extraction, and routing tasks rarely need frontier models. Smaller, cheaper models handle these well.
  • Complex reasoning, nuanced writing, and multi-step analysis benefit from more capable models — and the quality difference is usually visible.
  • If you're building a pipeline with multiple steps, you can often use a cheaper model for early filtering stages and a more capable model only for the final output.
  • Fine-tuned smaller models often outperform general frontier models on domain-specific tasks — and cost a fraction of the price per call.

Open-Weight Models and Private Hosting

The calculator focuses on hosted API providers, but it's worth knowing that open-weight models — Llama, Mistral, Phi, and others — can be self-hosted or run privately, which changes the cost structure entirely. Instead of paying per token, you pay for compute. For high-volume workloads, this often works out significantly cheaper. For low-volume or irregular workloads, hosted APIs are usually more practical.

Private hosting also means your data never leaves your infrastructure. For businesses handling sensitive documents, financial records, or client data, that's not a minor consideration — it's often the deciding factor.

What This Calculator Doesn't Cover

To be honest about the limits: this tool compares API costs. It doesn't account for the engineering time to build and maintain a pipeline, the cost of errors or retries, embedding costs if you're using RAG, or the infrastructure costs of self-hosting. A complete cost picture needs all of those. This calculator helps with one important part of it.

It also doesn't tell you which model is best for your specific task. That requires testing on your actual data and your actual use case. Cost comparison is a useful input to that decision — it's not a substitute for it.

If You're Building Something at Scale

If you're at the stage where LLM costs are a meaningful line item — or you're trying to figure out whether a particular approach is commercially viable — it's worth thinking through the full architecture before you commit. The choice of provider, model, and pipeline structure all affect cost, and those decisions are easier to make at the design stage than after you've built everything around a particular setup.

At FineTuning, we work across multiple providers and open-weight models, and we don't have a financial interest in steering you towards any particular one.
